background_notes.fact: For a jointly smooth map u on ℝ^n×(0,∞) with finite positive dimensions, its density e=|u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² is smooth and ∂_t e=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t.

grounds.reason: n and m are positive finite integer dimensions.
All component derivatives are smooth on the open domain.
e is exactly this finite sum of Euclidean squares.

background_notes.justification: Expand each squared norm as the sum of the squares of its m real components. The ordinary one-variable product rule in time differentiates each square to twice the component times its time derivative. Smoothness implies continuous second partial derivatives, so Schwarz's mixed-partial equality identifies ∂_t∂_{x_j}u with ∂_{x_j}u_t. Finite summation gives the displayed formula and smoothness.

background_notes.fact: For R>0 and t0>0, η=t0/4 gives a compact set K=[−R,R]^n×[t0−η,t0+η] lying in ℝ^n×(0,∞); any continuous real function g on that domain has |g|≤B on K for some finite B≥0.

grounds.reason: R>0 is available and e_t is jointly continuous.
t0 is fixed positive and Q=[−R,R]^n.
η=t0/4, so the closed time interval lies in int J and is positive.

background_notes.justification: K is a closed bounded box in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, hence compact by Heine–Borel. Absolute value composed with a continuous g is continuous; its image of K is compact in ℝ and consequently bounded. A nonnegative bound follows, including when g vanishes identically. Apply this to g=e_t to obtain the F002 witness.

background_notes.fact: The box Q=[−R,R]^n is Lebesgue measurable. For finite B0≥0 and finite Lebesgue measure μ(Q), B0·1_Q is absolutely integrable with integral B0 μ(Q).

grounds.reason: Q is this finite box and μ(Q)=(2R)^n is finite.
F002 supplies a finite nonnegative B0, chosen at S003.
1_Q is explicitly one on Q and zero off Q.

background_notes.justification: Q is closed, so it is Borel and Lebesgue measurable. The indicator is a measurable simple function and its integral is μ(Q) by the definition of integration for indicators. Scaling by finite B0 gives the stated finite integral of its absolute value.

background_notes.fact: Under L1, every Fseq(k)(x)=[e(x,t0+hseq(k))−e(x,t0)]/hseq(k) is continuous in x and Lebesgue almost everywhere strongly measurable.

grounds.reason: e is jointly continuous and each positive-time slice is continuous.
L1 ensures hseq(k)≠0 and t0+hseq(k)>0 for all k.

background_notes.justification: Restriction to a positive-time slice preserves continuity. Subtraction and multiplication by the fixed real scalar 1/hseq(k) preserve continuity. A real-valued continuous function is Borel measurable and has separable range in ℝ. Measurable real functions admit pointwise simple-function approximations (truncate values and subdivide bounded ranges), giving strong measurability, hence almost everywhere strong measurability for Lebesgue measure.

background_notes.fact: If real f and g are absolutely Lebesgue integrable and h≠0, then (f−g)/h is absolutely integrable and ∫(f−g)/h=(∫f−∫g)/h. Finite scalar multiples and finite sums of absolutely integrable real functions are absolutely integrable.

grounds.reason: The density slices and each product in the output formula are absolutely integrable at the relevant positive times.
L1 supplies hseq(k)≠0 and positive shifted times.
E is the integral of the corresponding density.

background_notes.justification: The bound |(f−g)/h|≤(|f|+|g|)/|h| proves absolute integrability. Additivity and scalar homogeneity of the real Lebesgue integral for integrable functions yield the formula. The same bound and linearity applied finitely many times cover the displayed scaled products and sums in N003.

background_notes.fact: Let η>0 and let G be real-valued on {h:0<|h|<η}. If G(h_k)→L for every sequence with 0<|h_k|<η and h_k→0, then lim_{h→0,h≠0}G(h)=L locally in this domain.

grounds.reason: F005 proves convergence of the energy quotients for an arbitrary sequence under precisely L1.
The argument explicitly reduces failure of the punctured limit to bad increments in shrinking neighborhoods.

background_notes.justification: Failure of the limit gives ε>0 such that for every δ>0 some h satisfies 0<|h|<min(δ,η) and |G(h)−L|≥ε. Choose h_k with 0<|h_k|<min(η/2,1/(k+1)) and this same error lower bound. Classical choice is permitted; these witnesses tend to zero and contradict the assumed sequential convergence. This expands exactly the contradiction argument already supplied in S006.
